translationRepairs: She bore five sons—Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, Quyi, and Quying—each of whom rose to prominent office.
She bore five sons—Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, Quyi (逸), and Quying—each of whom rose to prominent office.
The second Quyi is 去逸, not 去疑, who is already the first Quyi.
She had five sons by the same father, named Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, Quyi, and Quying, all of whom became eminent officials.
She had five sons by the same father, named Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, Quyi (逸), and Quying, all of whom became eminent officials.
The second Quyi is 去逸, not 去疑.
It was Quyi who gave birth to the future empress.
It was Quyi (逸) who gave birth to the future empress.
去逸 is the son who fathered the empress, not 去疑, whom the English also spells Quyi.
去逸 is the son who fathered the empress, not 去疑.
On the Dragon Boat Festival he summoned the recluse Li Tang. Holding a young daughter, he said to Tang, "I miss him—don't be surprised."
On the Dragon Boat Festival he summoned the recluse Li Tang. Holding a young daughter, he said to Tang, "I am thinking of her—don't be surprised."
我念之 refers to the young daughter he is holding, not to an absent man. Li Tang then turns the remark toward the retired emperor.
On the Dragon Boat Festival the Emperor summoned the mountain recluse Li Tang; the Emperor was just then holding a young daughter and, turning to Tang, said: "I miss him—do not be surprised."

On the Dragon Boat Festival the Emperor summoned the mountain recluse Li Tang; the Emperor was just then holding a young daughter and, turning to Tang, said: "I am thinking of her—do not be surprised."
我念之 refers to the young daughter he is holding.
Once Daizong was enthroned, the ministers urged the dying emperor to depose her as a commoner and have her executed.
Once Daizong was enthroned, the ministers urged the emperor to depose her as a commoner and have her executed.
白帝 does not say the emperor was dying. Daizong has already taken the throne in this sentence.
When he saw the true grandson, he was overjoyed, held the child up to the sun, and said, "His fortune exceeds his father's."
When he saw the true grandson, he was overjoyed, gazed at him toward the sun, and said, "His fortune exceeds his father's."
向日視之 is looking at the child toward the sun, not lifting him up.

In the Tianbao era the Emperor was Prince of Guangping; at that time the Yang clan of Consort Yang was the most exalted among affinal kin, and Lady of Han state, wife of Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Xun, made her daughter the imperial grandson's consort.

In the Tianbao era the Emperor was Prince of Guangping; at that time the Yang clan of Consort Yang was the most exalted among affinal kin, and Lady of Han state, wife of Vice Director of the Palace Library Cui Xun, made her daughter the imperial grandson's consort.
秘書少監 belongs to the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat.
Three years later he ordered a tomb built west of the capital so he could see it each day.
Three years later he ordered a tomb built to the left of the capital so he could see it each day.
都左 is the left side of the capital. The literal already says left; west is not in the Chinese.

On Dezong's accession he first enfeoffed her forebears posthumously: great-great-grandfather Shiheng as Grand Guardian, great-grandfather Jiefu as Grand Tutor, father Yizhi as Grand Preceptor, brother Yiliang as Minister of Works, and Yizhi's son Zhen as Grand Marshal.

On Dezong's accession he first enfeoffed her forebears posthumously: great-grandfather Shiheng as Grand Guardian, grandfather Jiefu as Grand Tutor, father Yizhi as Grand Preceptor, younger brother Yiliang as Minister of Works, and Yizhi's son Zhen as Grand Marshal.
曾祖 is a great-grandfather, 祖 is a grandfather, and 弟 is a younger brother.

When Dezong took the throne, he first issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing the empress's great-great-grandfather Shiheng as Grand Guardian, her great-grandfather Jiefu as Grand Tutor, her father Yizhi as Grand Preceptor, her younger brother Yiliang as Minister of Works, and Yizhi's son Zhen as Grand Marshal.

When Dezong took the throne, he first issued an edict posthumously enfeoffing the empress's great-grandfather Shiheng as Grand Guardian, her grandfather Jiefu as Grand Tutor, her father Yizhi as Grand Preceptor, her younger brother Yiliang as Minister of Works, and Yizhi's son Zhen as Grand Marshal.
曾祖 is a great-grandfather and 祖 is a grandfather. The literal already says younger brother for 弟.

As the burial drew near, the Empress's stepmother, Lady Zheng of Zheng, asked to set up funeral offerings. The court replied that mourners need not lodge ritual goods in temporary quarters along the route—any who wished to sacrifice might do so.

As the burial drew near, the Empress's stepmother, Lady Zheng of Cheng, asked to set up funeral offerings. The court replied that mourners need not lodge ritual goods in temporary quarters along the route—any who wished to sacrifice might do so.
郕國 is the state of Cheng. 鄭 is the surname Zheng, not a second Zheng.

When the burial was imminent, the stepmother, Lady Zheng of the State of Zheng, requested that offerings be set out. An edict stated that sacrificial goods need not be lodged in temporary quarters; whoever wished to offer sacrifice was permitted to do so.

When the burial was imminent, the stepmother, Lady Zheng of the State of Cheng, requested that offerings be set out. An edict stated that sacrificial goods need not be lodged in temporary quarters; whoever wished to offer sacrifice was permitted to do so.
郕國 is Cheng, not the state of Zheng. 鄭 is her surname.
Both drafts were set aside, and Hanlin Academician Wu Tongxuan was ordered to rewrite the scroll, which then read "Empress Wang of Zi."
Both drafts were set aside, and Hanlin Academician Wu Tongxuan was ordered to rewrite the scroll, which then read "Empress Wang."
咨 in 咨後王氏 is an interjection, not a place or a name Zi.
Both were ordered revised, and the Hanlin academician Wu Tongxuan was commanded to rewrite the text; the scroll read "Empress Wang of Zi."
Both were ordered revised, and the Hanlin academician Wu Tongxuan was commanded to rewrite the text; the scroll read "Empress Wang."
咨 is an interjection, not Zi.
She began as a Lady of Excellent Character; in the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Dezong enfeoffed her as Consort Xian.
She began as a worthy companion; in the fourth year of Zhenyuan, Dezong enfeoffed her as Consort Xian.
良娣 is the rank worthy companion, not a personal quality called Excellent Character.
At first she was a Lady of Excellent Character; in the fourth year of Zhenyuan under Dezong she was enfeoffed as Consort Xian.
At first she was a worthy companion; in the fourth year of Zhenyuan under Dezong she was enfeoffed as Consort Xian.
良娣 is the rank worthy companion.
Her grandfather Nan De had won distinction in his generation.
Her grandfather Nande had won distinction in his generation.
難得 is a single given name, not Nan plus De.
After Wang entered the Eastern Palace as heir, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Excellent Character.
While the prince was in the Eastern Palace, she was enfeoffed as worthy companion.
王在東宮 is the prince in the Eastern Palace, not Empress Wang entering it. 良娣 is the rank worthy companion.
When Wang was in the Eastern Palace, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Excellent Character.
When the prince was in the Eastern Palace, she was enfeoffed as worthy companion.
王在東宮 is the prince in the Eastern Palace. 良娣 is the rank worthy companion.
When Xianzong yielded the throne in an inner abdication, she was honored as Grand Empress.
When the throne passed to Xianzong by an inner abdication, she was honored as Grand Empress.
憲宗內禪 is the abdication that made Xianzong emperor, not Xianzong giving the throne away.
When Xianzong abdicated in favor of his father, she was honored as Grand Empress.
When the inner abdication made Xianzong emperor, she was honored as Grand Empress.
Xianzong did not abdicate in favor of his father. 內禪 made him emperor.
Her father Guo Ai had married Princess Shengping, and it was he—not the princess—who was her true parent.
Her father Guo Ai had married Princess Shengping, and the princess bore the empress.
實生後, with 母素貴 and the later Grand Princess mother, means Princess Shengping bore her. The English reverses this.
Her father Guo Ai married Princess Shengping; it was he who actually bore the empress.
Her father Guo Ai married Princess Shengping; she actually bore the empress.
實生後 is the princess giving birth, not the father bearing her.
When Baoli died suddenly, the Grand Empress Dowager summoned the Prince of Jiang to the throne—he became Wenzong.
When the Baoli era ended suddenly, the Grand Empress Dowager summoned the Prince of Jiang to the throne—he became Wenzong.
寶歷 is the reign name, not a person who died.
Baoli passed suddenly; the empress dowager summoned the Prince of Jiang to succeed to the imperial throne—this was Wenzong.
The Baoli era ended suddenly; the empress dowager summoned the Prince of Jiang to succeed to the imperial throne—this was Wenzong.
寶歷 is the reign name, not a person.
Wuzong loved the hunt, wrestlers, and acrobatic performers, and chose boys from the Five Wards who were allowed to come and go within the inner palace.
Wuzong loved the hunt, wrestlers, and acrobatic performers, and chose boys from the Five Animal Services who were allowed to come and go within the inner palace.
五坊 is the five imperial animal-training services, not city wards.
Wuzong delighted in hunting excursions, wrestlers, and acrobats; he selected youths from the Five Wards who could enter and leave the forbidden inner palace.
Wuzong delighted in hunting excursions, wrestlers, and acrobats; he selected youths from the Five Animal Services who could enter and leave the forbidden inner palace.
五坊 is the five imperial animal-training services, not city wards.
When Xuanzong came to the throne, he was her son like the others by lineage, yet his mother was Lady Zheng—once a palace maid—and old grievances lay between them.
When Xuanzong came to the throne, toward the empress dowager he counted among the princes, but his mother was Lady Zheng—once a palace maid—and old grievances lay between them.
於後，諸子也，而母鄭 contrasts the princes with his real mother. Lady Zheng, not Empress Yi'an, bore him.
When Xuanzong ascended, by the empress dowager he was her son among her sons, but his mother was Lady Zheng, formerly a serving maid—with old resentment between them.
When Xuanzong ascended, in relation to the empress dowager he was one among the princes, but his mother was Lady Zheng, formerly a serving maid—with old resentment between them.
而母鄭 means Lady Zheng was his mother. The empress dowager was not.

The Director of Court Ceremonies Wang Hao requested that the empress dowager be jointly buried at Jing Mausoleum, with her spirit tablet enshrined in Xianzong's spirit chamber; the emperor was displeased and ordered Chancellor Bai Minzhong to reprove him.

Wang Hao, an official of the Court of Sacrifices requested that the empress dowager be jointly buried at Jing Mausoleum, with her spirit tablet enshrined in Xianzong's spirit chamber; the emperor was displeased and ordered Chancellor Bai Minzhong to reprove him.
太常官 is an official of the Court of Sacrifices, not its Director.
During the Changqing era she was enfeoffed as princess consort.
During the Changqing era she was enfeoffed as consort.
冊為妃 is the consort rank fei, not a princess consort.
During Changqing she was enfeoffed as princess consort.
During Changqing she was enfeoffed as consort.
冊為妃 is the consort rank fei, not a princess consort.

About then, Tang Fu, observation commissioner of Fujian, reported that a Quanzhou man named Xiao Hong had declared himself the Empress Dowager's brother. The Censorate looked into it and said he was not. Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi spoke up for him again and asked that he be examined face to face with the real brother. The throne ordered Gao Yuanyu, Sun Jian, and Cui Xun of the Three Offices to question them together—and both men were frauds.

About then, Tang Fu, observation commissioner of Fujian, reported that a Quanzhou man named Xiao Hong had declared himself the Empress Dowager's brother. The Censorate looked into it and said he was not. Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi spoke up for him again and asked that he be examined face to face with Ben. The throne ordered Gao Yuanyu, Sun Jian, and Cui Xun of the Three Offices to question them together—and both men were frauds.
請與本辨 means confront him with Xiao Ben, not with the true brother.

At that time Fujian Observation Commissioner Tang Fu memorialized: a Quanzhou man named Xiao Hong claimed to be the Empress Dowager's brother. The Censorate investigated and found it untrue. Zhaoyi Liu Congjian again spoke on his behalf and asked that he be confronted with the genuine claimant. An edict ordered the Three Offices—Gao Yuanyu, Sun Jian, and Cui Xun—to conduct a joint inquiry; both claims proved false.

At that time Fujian Observation Commissioner Tang Fu memorialized: a Quanzhou man named Xiao Hong claimed to be the Empress Dowager's brother. The Censorate investigated and found it untrue. Zhaoyi Liu Congjian again spoke on his behalf and asked that he be confronted with Ben. An edict ordered the Three Offices—Gao Yuanyu, Sun Jian, and Cui Xun—to conduct a joint inquiry; both claims proved false.
本 is Xiao Ben. The true brother is still unnamed, and both claims are then found false.
The real brother was exiled to Aizhou and Hong to Danzhou, and the Empress Dowager never got her brother back.
Ben was exiled to Aizhou and Hong to Danzhou, and the Empress Dowager never got her brother back.
本流愛州 exiles Xiao Ben. The true brother is not the man sent to Aizhou.
The genuine [brother] was banished to Aizhou, Hong to Danzhou, and the Empress Dowager never recovered her brother.
Ben was banished to Aizhou, Hong to Danzhou, and the Empress Dowager never recovered her brother.
本 is Xiao Ben, and 弘 is the Quanzhou claimant Xiao Hong, not the true brother.

At first, in the Dahe years, Empress Dowager Yi'an lived in Xingqing Palace and Empress Dowager Baoli in Yi'an Hall; later they moved into the inner palace and were called the "Three-Palace Empresses Dowager".

At first, in the Dahe years, Empress Dowager Yi'an lived in Xingqing Palace and Empress Dowager Baoli in Yi'an Hall; and this empress dowager lived in the Great Inner Palace; the three were called the "Three-Palace Empresses Dowager".
後居大內 means this empress dowager lived in the Great Inner Palace. 後 is not the adverb later, and the three did not move together.

Initially, in the Dahe era, Empress Dowager Yi'an resided in Xingqing Palace and Empress Dowager Baoli in Yi'an Hall; later they lived within the Great Inner Palace and were styled the "Three-Palace Empresses Dowager".

Initially, in the Dahe era, Empress Dowager Yi'an resided in Xingqing Palace and Empress Dowager Baoli in Yi'an Hall; and this empress dowager lived in the Great Inner Palace and the three were styled the "Three-Palace Empresses Dowager".
後 is the empress dowager, not later. Each dowager has her own residence.
During the Changqing era she was enfeoffed as princess consort.
During the Changqing era she was enfeoffed as consort.
冊為妃 is the consort rank fei, not a princess consort.
During Changqing she was enfeoffed as princess consort.
During Changqing she was enfeoffed as consort.
冊為妃 is the consort rank fei, not a princess consort.
He then also asked the chief ministers: "Is it better to bury her following Guangling, or only to enshrine her spirit tablet in the ancestral temple?"
He then also asked the chief ministers: "Is it better to bury her following the Guang mausoleum, or only to enshrine her spirit tablet in the ancestral temple?"
光陵 is Muzong's Guang mausoleum, not the princely fief 廣陵.
Through the three reigns of Xianzong, Muzong, and Jingzong, all called her "Elder"; empresses, consorts, princes, and princesses all met her with the rites due a teacher.
Through the three reigns of Xianzong, Muzong, and Jingzong, all called her "Master"; empresses, consorts, princes, and princesses all met her with the rites due a teacher.
先生 here is Master, the teacher they bowed to, not a relative's age.

In the Dahe era, Li Xun and Zheng Zhu held power; they hated Chancellor Li Zongmin and slandered him, saying that through Imperial Son-in-law Shen Cai's heavy bribes to Ruoxian she had sought the chancellorship.

In the Dahe era, Li Xun and Zheng Zhu held power; they hated Chancellor Li Zongmin and slandered him, saying that through Imperial Son-in-law Shen Cai's heavy bribes to Ruoxian he had sought the chancellorship.
求執政 is the charge against Li Zongmin, not against Ruoxian.

Before a year had passed she was raised to Honored Consort; her father Yi was posthumously made Minister of Rites, her brother Huan Vice Director of the Palace Workshops, and a great house was bestowed on the family.

The next year she was raised to Honored Consort; her father Yi was posthumously made Minister of Rites, her brother Huan Vice Director of the Palace Workshops, and a great house was bestowed on the family.
逾年 means the next year, not before a year had passed.
Within the year she became Honored Consort; Yi was posthumously made Minister of Rites; her brother Huan was made Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service; a great mansion was granted.
The next year she became Honored Consort; Yi was posthumously made Minister of Rites; her brother Huan was made Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service; a great mansion was granted.
逾年 means the next year, not within the year.
When Xuanzong ascended, he praised her integrity, posthumously enfeoffed her Worthy Consort, and buried her in Bocheng of Duanling.
When Xuanzong ascended, he praised her integrity, posthumously enfeoffed her Worthy Consort, and buried her in the cypress enclosure of Duanling.
柏城 is the mausoleum's cypress enclosure, not a place named Bocheng.
Later, when princes Kui, Zhao, and five others still lived in the inner court, Yun alone was sent out to establish his own household.
Later, when the five princes, Kui and Zhao among them still lived in the inner court, Yun alone was sent out to establish his own household.
等五王 is five princes in all, not Kui, Zhao, and five more.
Later princes Kui and Zhao and the other five dwelt in the inner court, but Yun alone left the inner quarters.
Later the five princes, Kui and Zhao among them dwelt in the inner court, but Yun alone left the inner quarters.
等五王 is five princes in all, not five besides Kui and Zhao.
In the fourteenth year Wang took the throne—he who became Xizong.
In the fourteenth year the prince took the throne—he who became Xizong.
王即位 is the prince, Prince Pu, not a man named Wang. He is Xizong.
In the fourteenth year Wang ascended—this was Xizong.
In the fourteenth year the prince ascended—this was Xizong.
王 is the prince, not the surname Wang.

When Wang took the throne as Zhaozong he posthumously made her Empress Dowager, gave her a temple name, installed her tablet in Yizong's shrine, and kept her existing tomb as Anling; he also summoned her younger brother Min and gave him office.

When the prince took the throne as Zhaozong he posthumously made her Empress Dowager, gave her a temple name, installed her tablet in Yizong's shrine, and kept her existing tomb as Anling; he also summoned her younger brother Min and gave him office.
王立 is Prince Shou, not a man surnamed Wang. He is Zhaozong.

When Wang ascended—this was Zhaozong—posthumously titled Empress Dowager, given posthumous name, tablet paired in Yizong's chamber, the former burial called Anling; summoned the Empress Dowager's younger brother Min to office.

When the prince ascended—this was Zhaozong—posthumously titled Empress Dowager, given posthumous name, tablet paired in Yizong's chamber, the former burial called Anling; summoned the Empress Dowager's younger brother Min to office.
王立 is the prince, not the surname Wang.
Once he became emperor, she was made Shufei.
Once he became emperor, she was made Worthy-and-Gentle Consort.
淑妃 is the consort rank, left untranslated as Shufei.
After he took the throne, she was titled Shufei.

unresolvedReferences.description: 以孺人為妃，後為良娣 can be read as the same lady later becoming a worthy companion, which is how the English reads 後. s0012 then distinguishes the consort who was cut off from the worthy companion. s0009 is not used as evidence that Wei Yuangui's daughter became the worthy companion. The worthy companion is Empress Zhang.
二年 names no reign. It follows 乾元初, but the unit itself is not converted to Qianyuan 2.
The son's name is the missing-glyph mark 〓. The English Shao is a translator's reading, not a character printed in the Chinese. He is not identified with the son born at Lingwu in s0017.
The son born at Lingwu is not named and is not identified with Shao or Tong.
弟清、潛尚大寧、延和二郡主 lists two brothers and two commandery princesses. The pairing Qing with Daning and Qian with Yanhe follows list order and is marked strongly inferred.
代宗已立，群臣白帝 does not say whether 帝 is the dying Suzong or Daizong. The idiomatic 'dying emperor' is repaired. The request is not treated as evidence that Suzong was still the reigning emperor.
A second empress, Zhangjing Wu, is introduced for Suzong after Zhang was empress. This chunk does not say when Wu received the title or reconcile the two empresses.
Five girls from Jingzhao are an undifferentiated group and are not made people. The other two of the three who were chosen are not named.
The wet nurse and the substituted palace child are unnamed functionaries, not individuated relatives, and are not made people.
Wu died at eighteen. That age is not converted into a birth year.
Dugu's native place is explicitly unknown (失其何所人). None is inferred.
The title is written 召王. The English says Prince of Zhao. Zhao is kept as the packet's English and is not treated as the character 趙.
後三年 is three years after the Dali 10 death, converted as AD 778. It is not a new reign name. 後 here means afterward, not the empress.
The heading calls Shen Empress Ruizhen, while the narrative says she was lost and does not record a posthumous grant in this chunk. The heading title is not dated.

The idiomatic English calls 曾祖 a great-great-grandfather and 祖 a great-grandfather. Both fields are repaired. The offices are posthumous grants at Dezong's accession and are not the ancestors' active years.
Emperor Xuan in the English is Dezong. The Chinese says 宣皇帝, an epithet, and is not a separate person.
Several women claimed to be the empress dowager. They are an undifferentiated plural and are not individuated.
外高祖 is a maternal great-great-grandfather, generation distance 4. The English great-great-grandfather matches. The grant year is not Lin's lifetime.
厭代二十有七年 is a duration. AD 778 is only the external accession year 805 minus 27, not a year the chapter names.
Empress Wang's genealogy is explicitly lost (失其譜系). None is inferred. 子姓姻出 are unnamed sons and affines.
郕國鄭夫人 is Lady Zheng, titled with the state Cheng. The English of Zheng is repaired. She is a stepmother, not a birth mother.
咨後王氏 addresses Empress Wang. 咨 is not the name Zi.
皇后長孫氏 is the wording of Empress Wende's scroll, so Changsun and Wende are one person. Cen Wenben and Wende are remembered from outside this reign; AD 636 is external.
The candidate 貞元 inside 永貞元年 is a character fragment, not a second Zhenyuan date. The era in this sentence is Yongzhen.
良娣 is a rank. The English Lady of Excellent Character is repaired.
難得 is one name. The English Nan De is repaired to Nande. Surfaces still use the packet spelling.

王在東宮 is the prince (Shunzong) in the Eastern Palace. The English makes Wang the person who entered and is repaired. 良娣 is again translated Lady of Excellent Character and is repaired to worthy companion. The English token Wang on this unit is not her name.
憲宗內禪 means the abdication that enthroned Xianzong. Both English fields had him abdicating and are repaired.
十一年 names no reign. It is not converted to Yuanhe 11. She was fifty-four. That age is not a birth year.
實生後 means Princess Shengping bore Empress Guo. The idiomatic claim that the father, not the princess, was the parent is repaired. Her mother is the same princess later called Grand Princess of Qi.
八年 names no reign. It follows 元和元年 but is not converted to Yuanhe 8.
The second brother's name is 鏦 followed by a non-character mark. The English Cong is kept as the packet reading and is not a restored character.
武氏 is Empress Wu, cited only as a model the dowager refuses. Her reign AD 690-705 is external.
寶歷 is a reign name. The English treated it as a person who died and is repaired. AD 826 is the external end of Baoli.
於後，諸子也，而母鄭 means Xuanzong stood among the princes in relation to Empress Yi'an, while his mother was Lady Zheng. The English made him her son and is repaired. She is not given a mother-child claim.
Her sudden death is placed the night Xuanzong took offense. The chapter gives no year. AD 846 is only his accession, external, and is not entered as a stated death year. AD 848 is not used.
咸通中 is the middle of Xiantong, AD 860-874, not a numbered year.
丹楊 is the packet's spelling. 或言本爾硃氏 is only a reported original clan, kept as an uncertain alternate and not merged away. The character is 硃, as written.
元和初 is not converted to Yuanhe 2. AD 806 is only the external start of Yuanhe.
妃 is consort, not princess consort. Changqing is the era AD 821-824, with no numbered year.
In Dahe 5 the Grand Empress Dowager is Empress Yi'an and the Baoli Empress Dowager is Empress Gongxi Wang, retitled from Yian Hall. Zheng is not yet dowager. 義安 is kept as the packet's Yian.
光陵 is Muzong's Guang mausoleum. The English Guangling is that tomb, not the princely fief 廣陵.
蕭洪 is the first false brother. An unnamed elder sister is implied by 姊婿呂璋 and is given her own record. Neither is the true brother.
蕭弘 is a second Xiao Hong, not 蕭洪. 請與本辨 confronts him with Xiao Ben, not with the true brother. 崔郇 is the packet's Cui Xun. The English real brother is repaired.
本流愛州，弘儋州 exiles Xiao Ben and Xiao Hong (弘). The English called Ben the real brother and is repaired. The true brother is the man she never recovered.

後居大內 is this empress dowager in the Great Inner Palace, beside Yi'an at Xingqing and Baoli at Yian Hall. The English read 後 as later and is repaired. She is Empress Zhenxian Xiao from the continuing biography; 蕭 is not rewritten in this stretch.
中元 is only the middle of 大中元年 and is not an era. Dazhong 1 is AD 847, external.

The two younger sisters are not named and are not distinguished from each other, so they are one family-summary of count 2 plus the lady enfeoffment, not two invented people. Wei was already dead. AD 840 is Wuzong's accession, not a stated death year.
The ministers say Guangling has stood twenty years. That is not converted into a calendar year.
韋宣文君, Confucius, 曹大家, 顏, and 冉 appear only inside the Women's Analects. 曹大家 is Ban Zhao and 顏 is Yan Hui, both external. Which 冉 is not stated. Their dates are not the Zhenyuan date of the book.
元和末 is not a numbered year. AD 820 is only the external end of Yuanhe.
先生 is Master. The literal Elder is repaired and is not a relative age.
寶歷初 is not a numbered year. AD 825 is only the external start of Baoli.
沈〓 has a missing glyph. Shen Cai is the packet's English and is not a restored character. The year Li Xun and Zheng Zhu fell is not stated, so AD 835 is not used.
逾年 is the next year. Both English fields said within the year and are repaired.
The year of Consort Guo's death is explicitly unknown and is not supplied from outside.
She entered the palace at thirteen. That age is not turned into a birth year.
開成末 is the end of Kaicheng. AD 840 is Wuzong's accession, external, not a numbered Kaicheng year.
The dying emperor is Wuzong from the continuing biography. 武宗 is not rewritten. AD 846 is external.
柏城 is the cypress enclosure of Duanling. The literal Bocheng is repaired.
夔、昭等五王 is five princes, two of them named. The English added five others and is repaired. The other three are not named and are not given separate identities. Their parentage is not stated.
Outsiders suspected Yizong was not the eldest. s0288 later calls the prince the legitimate eldest. The chapter contradicts itself, so neither unit is used as a birth-order claim.
安王 is a fragment across 惠安 and 王皇后, not a prince of An. Her origins are unknown.
七年 names no reign. It is not converted to Xiantong 7.
十四年 names no reign and is not converted. 王 is Prince Pu, who is Xizong. The English Wang is repaired. AD 873 is only his external accession.
The rumor that Consort Guo and Wei Baoheng were intimate is explicitly unproved and is not a relationship.
Consort Guo's end is unknown and is not supplied. AD 880 for Huang Chao's rebellion is external; the chapter gives no year.
王立 is Prince Shou, who is Zhaozong, not a surname Wang. The younger brother's name is the missing-glyph mark 〓. Min is the packet's English only. AD 888 is external.
The packet writes 硃全忠. That character is kept and not normalized to 朱.
Zhaozong's murder has no year in the chapter. AD 904 is external.
Empress He was killed as Ai prepared to abdicate. AD 905 is external and is not written here. 母子 is read as herself and Emperor Ai.
She was strangled and degraded to commoner. The shameful name is not quoted, so it is not recorded as a name.
